A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pharmacology of synaptic GABA(A) receptor (GABAR) currents in CA1 hippocampal pyramidal neurons is differentially altered by chronic intermittent ethanol (EtOH) treatment in a manner consistent with a switch in GABAR subunit composition.

chronic alcohol treatment causes a switch in the subunit composition of GABAARs in the brain, leading to a change in the pharmacological profile of GABAergic transmission that could contribute to the behavioral and neurochemical changes associated with alcohol dependence.

alcohol dependence is associated with altered GABAergic signaling in the brain.
there is an important role of GABAARs in the brain changes that occur in alcohol dependence.
